body.rationale: The governing IPS is still a draft, so I weighted compliance only as a soft guide. I ranked on how usable each portfolio is for the CIO. 1) cvar_minimization: it has no hard IPS breach and the best backtest Sharpe in the field (0.74). Its -18.7% drawdown is well inside the -25% limit and its CRO score is moderate (0.41). It is tail- and covariance-driven, which fits the late-cycle lesson in §4.3. The reviews found no technical error, only a thin tail sample and a return target tuned to the 8% volatility floor. 2) black_litterman: it is compliant, with backtest Sharpe 0.70, effective N of 6.1 and 3.0% tracking error. The reviewers' flagged gamma-direction inconsistency is a reporting problem, not a flaw in the weights. 3) pc_researcher: it has the best ex-ante Sharpe (0.51), a contained drawdown (-10.9%) and a low CRO score (0.33). It breaches volatility and tracking error only, which a draft IPS can revisit. Reviewers noted an unexplained Sharpe above max_sharpe's and a mis-stated volatility constraint, which keeps it at third. 4) max_sharpe: it is compliant with decent backtest Sharpe, but 46% sits in us_value on a modest CMA spread and the drawdown is -24.7%, so it is a weaker base. 5) inverse_volatility: it is forecast-free, holds 18 assets, has a -9% drawdown and gives the ensemble a heuristic, covariance-based voice. It breaches the volatility, return and tracking-error limits, and reviewers caught its effective-N and CMA-independence misstatements. My first choice beats my fifth because cvar_minimization meets the IPS volatility band and return target with a far higher backtest Sharpe (0.74 vs 0.57), while inverse_volatility earns 5.0% at 3.1% volatility and misses the mandate. Together the five span the non_traditional, return_optimized, pc_researcher and heuristic families. I flagged market_cap_weight: it has the highest CRO risk (0.80) and a -40.6% backtest drawdown, far past the -25% limit. Reviewers also said an ETF-AUM proxy is mislabelled as the market portfolio and its concentration statistics are inconsistent. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, because its orthogonality has ensemble value even though it breaches the IPS.
